title: Rice protein
description: Inorganic arsenic, cadmium, mercury and lead evidence for brown rice protein and other rice protein powders, with sample-level FDA and WHO GEMS/Food results, applicable limits and what a buyer should ask a supplier.
lede: Rice protein carries inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium: 17 of 19 US rice protein samples had quantified inorganic arsenic, all 22 powders in WHO monitoring from the Americas had quantified lead, and the only cadmium figure is for rice endosperm protein.

answers.text: Inorganic arsenic is supported by 19 FDA samples and lead by 22 GEMS/Food results; cadmium by one endosperm protein study and a Canadian survey statement; mercury by one sample.

citation_spans.after: Inorganic arsenic is supported by 19 FDA samples and lead by 22 GEMS/Food results; cadmium by one endosperm protein study and a Canadian survey statement; mercury by one sample.

answers.text: Lot testing for inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium deserves priority, and the material type matters: in a small comparison, powders labeled brown rice protein had higher inorganic arsenic than those labeled rice protein.

citation_spans.after: Lot testing for inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium deserves priority, and the material type matters: in a small comparison, powders labeled brown rice protein had higher inorganic arsenic than those labeled rice protein.

answers.text: The limiting gaps are growing origin, cadmium in brown rice protein, which has no quantified result, and lead results from outside the Americas.

citation_spans.after: The limiting gaps are growing origin, cadmium in brown rice protein, which has no quantified result, and lead results from outside the Americas.

presentation.text: Inorganic arsenic is the best-documented metal in rice protein: FDA sampled 19 rice protein powders from US retail in its 2012 to 2013 rice survey, and 17 had quantified inorganic arsenic between 25 and 152 µg/kg, with a median of 47 µg/kg (an Index calculation). The other two had total arsenic below the 10 µg/kg detection limit.

citation_spans.after: Inorganic arsenic is the best-documented metal in rice protein: FDA sampled 19 rice protein powders from US retail in its 2012 to 2013 rice survey, and 17 had quantified inorganic arsenic between 25 and 152 µg/kg, with a median of 47 µg/kg (an Index calculation).
The other two had total arsenic below the 10 µg/kg detection limit.

passages.text: Cadmium is the second concern: five batches of rice endosperm protein made in Japan averaged 0.14 mg/kg with a standard deviation of 0.17 mg/kg, and a Canadian survey reported that rice-based protein powders had the highest metal levels of the protein types it tested, especially cadmium. One brown rice protein powder in that survey had 0.022 ppm mercury, the survey maximum.

citation_spans.after: Cadmium is the second concern: five batches of rice endosperm protein made in Japan averaged 0.14 mg/kg with a standard deviation of 0.17 mg/kg, and a Canadian survey reported that rice-based protein powders had the highest metal levels of the protein types it tested, especially cadmium.
One brown rice protein powder in that survey had 0.022 ppm mercury, the survey maximum.

passages.text: Lead was quantified in all 22 rice protein powders that WHO GEMS/Food holds from the Americas, sampled at random and reported for 2014 and 2017: 110 to 445 µg/kg dry weight, median 241 µg/kg (an Index calculation). No result is linked to where the rice was grown, so China, Vietnam, the USA and Canada cannot be compared as origins. For a buyer, that makes lot testing for inorganic arsenic, lead and cadmium the decision point rather than origin.

presentation.text: This page covers protein isolated or concentrated from rice, including brown rice protein, sold as powder or used as an ingredient. FDA classified 12 samples as rice protein powders and included 7 more rice protein products under protein beverages, measured as powder before mixing. WHO GEMS/Food records its lead results under products for special nutritional use, with each powder named as sold. The cadmium study used rice endosperm protein made from milled rice flour, which is a different fraction from brown rice protein.
